title: Parametrically Enhanced Ergotropy and Charging Power in a Three-Mode Bosonic Quantum Battery
abstract: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. We show that active parametric driving drastically increases the stored energy and peak charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping in the battery. We achieve a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in the battery's stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We also analyze the effects of pure dephasing on the charging power, ergotropy, and extractable work quality.. Although two--photon pumping introduces photon--number fluctuations that slightly lower the fractional ergotropy ratio ${\cal W}_{\rm B}/{\cal E}_{\rm B}$, the absolute extractable work remains substantially elevated compared to unassisted configurations.
summary: The authors propose a theoretical scheme to boost the performance of a quantum battery by integrating a degenerate optical parametric amplifier (OPA). By modeling the three-mode system using the Lindblad master equation, they demonstrate that active parametric driving significantly increases the stored energy and extractable work. This research highlights how engineered quantum sources can enhance energy transfer efficiency in quantum devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is to theoretically enhance the ergotropy (extractable work) and charging power of a quantum battery system.
main_result: Active parametric driving using a degenerate OPA achieves a multi-order-of-magnitude boost in stored energy and charging power while maintaining nonreciprocal energy trapping.
method: The analysis uses a strictly open-quantum-system framework derived from the Lindblad master equation to track expectation values and dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a three-mode bosonic quantum battery: a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary mediator cavity, and an energy-storage battery cavity. An OPA is integrated into the charger cavity to act as an active energy source.
key_observables: Stored energy ($E_B, E_{ch}$), peak charging power ($P_B$), Ergotropy ($W_B$), and the energy ratio ($\xi_{13}$).
important_parameters: OPA gain ($\lambda$), pump phase, coupling phases, and pure dephasing rates ($\gamma_p$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using the Lindblad master equation, and the analysis accounts for fluctuations introduced by the two-photon pumping process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic system setup, the OPA process, and show how increasing OPA gain enhances charging power and ergotropy, while pure dephasing degrades these metrics.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model, derives the dynamics via the Lindblad master equation, analyzes the effect of parametric driving on energy transfer and work extraction, and finally assesses the robustness against decoherence mechanisms like pure dephasing.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines quantum optics (OPA, cavity QED) with open quantum system dynamics (Lindblad equation) to model energy storage, a key area in quantum information science and quantum thermodynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: (a) Schematic representation of the system battery under consideration. (b) The system utilizes a degenerate OPA process where, mediated by second-order nonlinearity χ(2), a single pump photon of frequency ωp is converted into two cavity photons of frequency ω1 (signal and Idler with same frequency ω1). This process is governed by the resonance relation ωp = 2ω1.

FIG. 2: Dynamical evolution of the charging of the quantum battery. (a,b) Stored energies of the charger and battery, Ech and EB, without (λ = 0) (a) and with the OPA (λ/κ = 1) (b), respectively. (c,d) Corresponding energy ratios ξ13 = EB/Ech. The other parameters are the same as in the table I.
